newsitem.title: UK: Sullom Voe blockade starts to delay Brent loadings.
newsitem.headline: Sullom Voe blockade starts to delay Brent loadings.

text.p: The blockade of the Sullom Voe oil port by local Shetland fisherman has already delayed the loading schedule for Brent crude, a port official said on Tuesday.
The blockade, now in its second day, prevented a fully-loaded crude tanker from leaving the North Sea port on schedule today at 0700 local time (0600 GMT).
The protest could prevent a second tanker berthing at the port at the scheduled time of 1600 local time (1500 GMT) on Tuesday afternoon, the official said.
Fourteen shell fishing boats were blocking access to the port at midday on Tuesday.
"We're staying exactly where we are," a crew member of the prawn dredger "Winsome" told Reuters by mobile telephone.
A compulsory order or "special directive" was issued by the Shetland Islands Council late on Monday ordering the fishing boats to leave the port area by 0300 local time (0200 GMT) on Tuesday.
"The matter is now in the hands of the police," said a port official on Tuesday morning.
The crews of the boats said they would not leave the harbour until they have received legal documents from the police.
"We haven't been contacted by the police yet," the "Winsome" crew member told Reuters at midday.
The crews face criminal charges and civil penalties which may include the substantial costs of delaying huge ocean going oil tankers, local officials said.

A spokeswoman for Sullom Voe terminal operator BP said on Tuesday that if the port remained closed tankage was sufficient to store oil until the weekend without affecting production at Brent system fields.
The fishermen are protesting against unpaid compensation claims from the International Oil Pollution Compensation Fund (IOPCF) for damage caused to fishing grounds by the Braer tanker spill in 1993.
The Sullom Voe terminal handles one fifth of Britain's oil output and is the export terminal for world benchmark crude Brent blend.
